bio_en: Kostia (Kosti) Hambardzumian escaped arrest as a young revolutionary by working his passage to America on a cargo ship, studied practical economics there and became a zemstvo agronomist in a Russian province. Pictured with Aram, Vana Ishkhan, Torgom and Menak, he spoke at Khecho's burial in July 1915 and after the Russian withdrawal in 1917 led the local Armenian forces in Vaspurakan. In 1918 he directed the Salmast fighting with Samson and Levon Shaghoyan. On 22 July 1918, near Sain-Kala in Persia, he rode out with a few comrades to meet what he thought were British troops; they were fleeing Turkish soldiers, who killed him only hours before the British arrived.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: high.
